entries.sanskrit:
द्वा-विंशे कर्दमायादाद् यथादिष्टं हि विष्णुना ।

मनुर् दुहितरं देव- हूतिम् इत्य् उपवर्ण्यते ॥

एवम् आविष्कृतोऽभिष्टुतोऽशेषाणां गुणानां कर्मणां चोदय उत्कर्षो यस्य स सम्राण् मनुः । स-व्रीड इव स्व-कीर्ति-श्रवणात्, प्रत्याख्यान-शङ्कया वा तं मुनिम् उवाच । उपारतं निवृत्ति-निरतम् ॥१॥
word_for_word: dvā-viṃśe kardamāyādād yathādiṣṭaṃ hi viṣṇunā
in the twenty-second chapter Manu gave [his daughter] to Kardama, as Viṣṇu had ordained
manur duhitaraṃ deva- hūtim ity upavarṇyate
Manu’s daughter Devahūti is being described as given.
evam āviṣkṛto’bhiṣṭuto’śeṣāṇāṃ guṇānāṃ karmaṇāṃ codaya utkarṣo yasya sa samrāṇ manuḥ
Manu, whose excellence is made manifest through praise—the impetus and eminence of all qualities and deeds—is the emperor
sa-vrīḍa iva sva-kīrti-śravaṇāt pratyākhyāna-śaṅkayā vā
as though embarrassed to hear his own fame, or fearing a refusal
taṃ munim uvāca
he spoke to the sage
upārataṃ nivṛtti-niratam
“upāratam” means one who has withdrawn, intent on renunciation
entries.literal_english: In the twenty-second chapter Manu gives his daughter Devahūti in marriage to Kardama, as Viṣṇu had ordained. Manu, whose excellence is made manifest through praise—the impetus and eminence of all qualities and deeds—is the emperor. As though embarrassed to hear his own fame, or fearing a refusal, he spoke to the sage. “Upāratam” means one who has withdrawn, intent on renunciation.

entries.sanskrit: मदीया कन्या त्वया परिणेयेति विज्ञापयिष्यन् युष्मद् अस्मत्-संबन्धस् तावद् ईश्वरेण पूर्वम् एव घटित इत्य् आह---ब्रह्मेति सार्धाभ्याम् । आत्मनः परीप्सया पर्याप्तुम् इच्छया । छन्दो-मयस्य्आत्मनः पर्याप्तिः पालनं वेद-प्रवर्तनं तस्येच्छया । युष्मान् ब्राह्मणान् । तत्-त्राणाय ब्राह्मण-पालनाय । ब्रह्म ब्राह्मण-जातिः । क्षत्रं क्षत्रिय-जातिः॥२-३॥
word_for_word: madīyā kanyā tvayā pariṇeyeti vijñāpayiṣyan
intending to propose, “My daughter is to be married by you”
yuṣmad-asmat-saṃbandhas tāvad īśvareṇa pūrvam eva ghaṭita ity āha brahmeti sārdhābhyām
he says in these verses that the relationship between you and me was already arranged by the Lord
ātmanaḥ parīpsayā paryāptum icchayā
“Parīpsayā” means with the desire to protect; “paryāptum” means to sustain.
chando-mayasya ātmanaḥ paryāptiḥ pālanaṃ veda-pravartanaṃ tasya icchayā
the sustenance of the self consisting of the Vedas means their preservation and the propagation of Vedic teaching, according to His desire
yuṣmān brāhmaṇān
“you” means the brāhmaṇas
tat-trāṇāya brāhmaṇa-pālanāya
“for their protection” means for the protection of the brāhmaṇas
brahma brāhmaṇa-jātiḥ kṣatraṃ kṣatriya-jātiḥ
“brahma” means the brāhmaṇa class; “kṣatram” means the kṣatriya class
entries.literal_english: Intending to propose, “My daughter is to be married by you,” he explains that the relationship between you and me had already been arranged by the Lord. “Ātmanaḥ parīpsayā” means by the desire to protect Himself; “paryāptum” means to sustain. The Vedic form of the Lord is sustained by the propagation of the Veda, according to His desire. “You” means the brāhmaṇas; “for their protection” means for the protection of the brāhmaṇas. “Brahma” means the brāhmaṇa class; “kṣatram” means the kṣatriya class.

entries.sanskrit: एवं स देव एव रक्षति स्म । कोऽसौ ? यः सद्-असद्-आत्मकः सर्वात्मकः । तथाप्य् अव्ययो निर्विकारः ॥४॥
word_for_word: evaṃ sa deva eva rakṣati sma
thus that very Lord protected him
ko’sau yaḥ sad-asad-ātmakaḥ sarvātmakaḥ
who is He? He is constituted of both being and nonbeing, the Self of all
tathāpy avyayo nirvikāraḥ
nevertheless, He is imperishable and without change
entries.literal_english: Thus that very Lord protected him. Who is He? He is constituted of both being and nonbeing, the Self of all; nevertheless, He is imperishable and without change.

entries.sanskrit: विज्ञापयति---स भवान् इति सप्तभिः । दुहितुः स्नेहेन परिक्लिष्ट आत्मा यस्य । श्रावितं विज्ञापनम् ॥८॥
word_for_word: vijñāpayati sa bhavān iti saptabhiḥ
he makes his request in seven verses beginning with “sa bhavān”
duhituḥ snehena parikliṣṭa ātmā yasya
he whose mind was distressed by affection for his daughter
śrāvitaṃ vijñāpanam
“śrāvitam” means the proposal that was communicated
entries.literal_english: He makes his request in seven verses beginning with “sa bhavān.” His mind was distressed by affection for his daughter. “Śrāvitam” means the proposal that was communicated.

entries.sanskrit: प्रियव्रतोत्तानपदोः स्वसेति पुत्रिका-करण-शङ्का निरस्ता । मम सुतेति क्षत्र-कन्या तव योग्येति दर्शितम् ॥९॥
word_for_word: priyavratottānapadoḥ svasā iti putrikā-karaṇa-śaṅkā nirastā
the doubt that she was the sister of Priyavrata and Uttānapāda is removed
mama suteti kṣatra-kanyā tava yogyeti darśitam
the words “my daughter” show that she is a kṣatriya maiden suited to you
entries.literal_english: The doubt that she was the sister of Priyavrata and Uttānapāda is removed. The words “my daughter” show that she is a kṣatriya maiden suited to you.

entries.sanskrit: यस्य सावधि ब्रह्मचर्यं स उपकुर्वाणाः । मे प्रत्तां मया दत्ताम् ॥१४॥

“upakurvāṇaḥ” is one who observes celibacy until a prescribed point
me prattāṃ mayā dattām
“me prattām” means “given by me”
entries.literal_english: “Upakurvāṇaḥ” is one who observes celibacy until a prescribed point. “Me prattām” means “given by me.”

entries.sanskrit: अप्रत्ता चेति मय्य् एव कृत-निश्चयत्वात् कस्मैचित् प्रतिश्रुता च न भवतीत्य् अर्थः। आद्यः प्रथमः, ततः पूर्वं विवाहाभावात् । मुख्य इति वा ॥१५॥
word_for_word: aprattā ceti mayy eva kṛta-niścayatvāt kasmaicit pratiśrutā ca na bhavatīty arthaḥ
“if she had not been given [to you]”—the meaning is that, being firmly resolved upon me alone, she has not been promised to anyone else
ādyaḥ prathamaḥ tataḥ pūrvaṃ vivāhābhāvāt
“Ādyaḥ” means first or primary, since no marriage had taken place before this.
mukhya iti vā
or it means the chief one
entries.literal_english: “If she had not been given [to you]”—the meaning is that, being firmly resolved upon me alone, she has not been promised to anyone else. “Ādyaḥ” means first or primary, since there was no marriage before this; or it means the chief one.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact grouped source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: भूयाद् भवेत् । प्रतीतः गृभ्णामि ते सौभगत्वाय हस्तं मया पत्या [ऋ।वे। १०.८५.३६] इत्य्-आदि-मन्त्र-प्रसिद्धः । स्वयाङ्ग-कान्त्यैव । श्रियं भूषणादि-शोभाम् ॥१६॥
word_for_word: bhūyād bhavet
“bhūyāt” means “may it be”
pratītaḥ gṛbhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastaṃ mayā patyā ity-ādi-mantra-prasiddhaḥ
“Pratīta” refers to the well-known Vedic mantra beginning, “I take your hand for good fortune,” Ṛgveda 10.85.36, and the rest.
pratītaḥ gṛbhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastaṃ mayā patyā ṛ|ve| 10.85.36 ity-ādi-mantra-prasiddhaḥ
“Pratīta” refers to the well-known Vedic mantra beginning, “I take your hand for good fortune,” and the rest.
śriyaṃ bhūṣaṇādi-śobhām
“śriyam” means the splendor of ornaments and the like
entries.literal_english: “Bhūyāt” means “may it be.” “Pratīta” refers to the well-known Vedic mantra, “I take your hand for good fortune,” and the rest. “Svayaṅga-kāntyā” means by her own bodily beauty. “Śriyam” means the splendor of ornaments and the like.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact grouped source range preserved.
transliteration: bhūyād bhavet | pratītaḥ gṛbhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastaṃ mayā patyā [Ṛgveda 10.85.36] ity-ādi-mantra-prasiddhaḥ | svayāṅga-kāntyaiva | śriyaṃ bhūṣaṇādi-śobhām ||16||

entries.sanskrit: यां विलोक्य न्यपतत् । संमोहेन विमूढं व्याकुलं चेतो यस्य । क्वणब्ध्याम् अङ्घ्रिभ्यां शोभा यस्याः ॥१७॥
word_for_word: yāṃ vilokya nyapatat
seeing her, he fell down
saṃmohena vimūḍhaṃ vyākulaṃ ceto yasya
he whose mind was bewildered and agitated by delusion
kvaṇabdhyām aṅghribhyāṃ śobhā yasyāḥ
she whose feet were beautiful with their tinkling anklets
entries.literal_english: Seeing her, he fell down. His mind was bewildered and agitated by delusion. Her feet were beautiful with their tinkling anklets.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact grouped source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: तां ललनानां ललामं भूषण-भूताम् । असेवितौ श्रियश् चरणौ यैस् तैर् अदृष्टां द्रष्टुम् अप्य् अयोग्याम् । उच्चपद उत्तानपादस्य । अभियातां स्वयं प्राप्ताम् ॥१८॥
word_for_word: tāṃ lalanānāṃ lalāmaṃ bhūṣaṇa-bhūtām
she was the crest-jewel of women, an ornament among them
asevitau śriyaś caraṇau yais tair adṛṣṭāṃ draṣṭum apy ayogyām
those who had never served her feet—Lakṣmī’s own feet—had not seen her and were not even fit to see her
uccapada uttānapādasya
“Uccapadaḥ” means “of Uttānapāda.”
abhiyātāṃ svayaṃ prāptām
“abhiyātām” means one who had arrived of her own accord
entries.literal_english: She was the crest-jewel of women, an ornament among them. Those who had never served her feet—Lakṣmī’s own feet—had not seen her and were not even fit to see her. “Uccapadaḥ” means “of Uttānapāda.” “Abhiyātām” means one who had arrived of her own accord.

entries.sanskrit: भजिष्ये स्वीकरिष्ये । "यावद् अपत्योत्पत्तिस् तावद् गार्हस्थ्यं, ततः परं सन्न्यासः" इति भाषा-बन्धः समयः । तम् एवाह---यावद् आत्मनो मम तेजो गर्भं बिभृयात् । यद् वा, ममात्मनो देहाच् च्युतं तेजो वीर्यं बिभृयाद् इति । अतः परं पारमहंस्यं ज्ञानं तस्मिन् मुख्यान् शुक्लेन विष्णुना साक्षात् प्रकर्षेणोक्तान् अविहिंस्रान् हिंसा-रहितान् शमादीन् बहु यथा भवत्य् एवम् अनुष्ठेयान् मन्ये ॥१९॥
word_for_word: bhajiṣye svīkariṣye
“I will accept her”
yāvad apatya-utpattis tāvad gārhasthyaṃ tataḥ paraṃ sannyāsaḥ iti bhāṣā-bandhaḥ samayaḥ
the agreement is: “Householder life continues until offspring are born; after that, renunciation”
tam evāha yāvad ātmano mama tejo garbhaṃ bibhṛyāt
he explains this point: she will carry my potency in her womb until it develops
yad vā mama ātmano dehāc cyutaṃ tejo vīryaṃ bibhṛyād iti
or, she will carry the semen that has left my body
ataḥ paraṃ pāramahaṃsyaṃ jñānaṃ tasmin mukhyān śuklena viṣṇunā sākṣāt prakarṣeṇa uktān avihiṃsrān hiṃsā-rahitān śama-ādīn
after that I regard as primary the knowledge of the paramahaṃsa, and the nonviolent disciplines such as tranquility and the rest—taught directly and with excellence by Viṣṇu, the pure one
bahu yathā bhavati evam anuṣṭheyān manye
I regard them as practices to be performed abundantly
entries.literal_english: “I will accept her.” The agreement is expressed as follows: “Householder life continues until offspring are born; after that, renunciation.” He explains this very point: she will carry my potency in her womb until it develops. Or, she will carry the semen that has left my body. After that I regard as primary the knowledge of the paramahaṃsa, and the nonviolent disciplines such as tranquility and the rest—taught directly and with excellence by Viṣṇu, the pure one—as practices to be performed abundantly.

entries.sanskrit: ननु तव पितुः प्रजा-पतेर् आज्ञा सृष्टाव् एव न सन्न्यासे तत्राह---यत इति । संस्थास्यते च लयं यास्यति । वावेति एवार्थे । ऋण-त्रयापाकरणानन्तरं सन्न्यास एव मादृशानां भगवतोक्त इत्य् अर्थः ।
word_for_word: nanu tava pituḥ prajā-pater ājñā sṛṣṭāv eva na sannyāse tatra āha yata iti
one might object: your father, the Prajāpati, ordered creation, not renunciation; he answers with “yataḥ”
saṃsthāsyate ca layaṃ yāsyati
“saṃsthāsyate” means “will come to an end, will be dissolved”
vāveti evārthe
“Vā” is used in the emphatic sense of “indeed.”
ṛṇa-trayāpākaraṇānantaraṃ sannyāsa eva mādṛśānāṃ bhagavatoktaḥ ity arthaḥ
the Lord has taught that for people like me, renunciation is appropriate only after discharging the three debts
entries.literal_english: One might object: your father, the Prajāpati, ordered creation, not renunciation. He answers with “yataḥ.” “Saṃsthāsyate” means “will come to an end, will be dissolved.” “Vā” is used emphatically. The Lord has taught that for people like me, renunciation is appropriate only after discharging the three debts.

entries.sanskrit: हे उग्र-धन्वन् विदुर ! लुलुभे मुनेर् मुखेन प्रलोभ्यते स च । यद् वा, मुखेन प्रलोभितवान् ॥२१॥
word_for_word: he ugra-dhanvan vidura
“O powerful archer, Vidura”
lulubhe muner mukhena pralobhyate sa ca
Manu was enticed by the sage’s face.
yad vā mukhena pralobhitavān
or he [Manu] enticed the sage by his own face.
entries.literal_english: Manu was enticed by the sage’s face; or, he himself enticed the sage by his own face.

entries.sanskrit: स मनुः । अन्व् अनन्तरम् । महिष्याश् च व्यवसितं निश्चयं ज्ञात्वा ॥२२॥
word_for_word: sa manuḥ
“saḥ” means Manu
anv anantaram
“Anu” means immediately afterward.
mahiṣyāś ca vyavasitaṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā
knowing the queen’s determination as well
entries.literal_english: “Saḥ” means Manu. “Anu” means immediately afterward. He knew the queen’s determination as well.

entries.sanskrit: पारिबर्हान् विवाह-काले प्रदेयान् । भूषाः भूषणानि वासांसि परिच्छदान् गृहोपकरणानि च ॥२३॥
word_for_word: pāribarhān vivāha-kāle pradeyān
“pāribarhān” means gifts to be presented at the time of marriage
bhūṣāḥ bhūṣaṇāni vāsāṃsi paricchadān gṛhopakaraṇāni ca
“bhūṣāḥ” means ornaments, garments, and household furnishings
entries.literal_english: “Pāribarhān” means gifts to be presented at the time of marriage; “bhūṣāḥ” means ornaments, garments, and household furnishings.

entries.sanskrit: प्रत्तां दत्ताम् । सदृक्षाय सदृशाय । गता व्यथा चिन्ता यस्य । औत्कण्ट्ह्येन उन्मथितः क्षुभित आशयो यस्य ॥२४॥
word_for_word: prattāṃ dattām
“prattām” means given
sadṛkṣāya sadṛśāya
“sadṛkṣāya” means to one who is equal
gatā vyathā cintā yasya
“Gatavyathā” means one whose distress or anxiety has passed.
autkaṇṭhyena unmathitaḥ kṣubhita āśayo yasya
one whose heart was shaken and disturbed by intense longing
entries.literal_english: “Prattām” means given. “Sadṛkṣāya” means to one who is equal. “Gatavyathā” means one whose anxiety has gone; whose heart was shaken by intense longing.

entries.sanskrit: तस्या विरहं सोढुं हे अम्ब ! हे वत्से ! इति ब्रुवन् । सन्धिर् आर्षः । शिखाः केशान् आसिञ्चत् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: tasyā virahaṃ soḍhuṃ he amba he vatse iti bruvan
speaking, “O mother! O daughter!” in order to bear her separation
sandhir ārṣaḥ
the construction is an archaic sandhi
śikhāḥ keśān āsiñcat
“śikhāḥ” means the hair; he sprinkled them
entries.literal_english: Speaking, “O mother! O daughter!” in order to bear her separation. The construction is an archaic sandhi. “Śikhāḥ” means the hair; he sprinkled them.

entries.sanskrit: अभिप्रेत्य ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मावर्ताद् देशात् प्रजाः पतिं प्रत्युज्जग्मुः ॥२८॥
word_for_word: abhipretya jñātvā
“abhipretya” means having understood
brahmāvartād deśāt prajāḥ patiṃ pratyujjagmuḥ
from the land of Brahmāvarta, the people came forth to welcome their lord
entries.literal_english: “Abhipretya” means having understood. From the land of Brahmāvarta, the people came forth to welcome the lord of progeny.

entries.sanskrit: कोऽसौ ब्रह्मावर्तः ? इत्य् अपेक्षायाम् आह---यत्र बर्हिष्मती नाम पुरीति । सापि कुत्र ? यत्र यज्ञस्य यज्ञ-वराहस्य रोमाणि न्यपतन्न् इति । यत्रेति सर्वत्र संबध्यते ॥२९॥
word_for_word: ko’sau brahmāvartaḥ ity apekṣāyām āha yatra barhiṣmatī nāma purīti
if one asks, “What is Brahmāvarta?” he says, “where the city named Barhiṣmatī is”
sāpi kutra yatra yajñasya yajña-varāhasya romāṇi nyapatann iti
and where is that? “Where the hairs of Yajña, the Boar, fell.”
yatreti sarvatra saṃbadhyate
the word “yatra” is connected everywhere
entries.literal_english: If one asks, “What is Brahmāvarta?” he says, “where the city named Barhiṣmatī is.” And where is that? “Where the hairs of Yajña, the Boar, fell.” The word “yatra” is connected everywhere.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact grouped source range preserved.
transliteration: ko’sau brahmāvartaḥ ? ity apekṣāyām āha---yatra barhiṣmatī nāma purīti | sāpi kutra ? yatra yajñasya yajña-varāhasya romāṇi nyapatann iti | yatreti sarvatra saṃbadhyate ||29||

entries.sanskrit: बर्हिष्मती नाम निरुक्तिं ब्रुवन् प्रसङ्गाद् देशस्य श्रैष्ठ्यम् आह द्वाभ्याम् । कुशाः काशाश् चासन् । शश्वन् नित्यं हरितं वर्चो वर्णो येषाम् । यज्ञ-घान् राक्षसादीन् । पराभवं नीत्वा यज्ञं विष्णुम् ॥३०॥
word_for_word: barhiṣmatī nāma niruktiṃ bruvan prasaṅgād deśasya śraiṣṭhyam āha dvābhyām
explaining the derivation of the name Barhiṣmatī, he also praises the excellence of the land in two verses
kuśāḥ kāśāś cāsan
kuśa grass and kāśa grass grew there
śaśvan nityaṃ haritaṃ varco varṇo yeṣām
their green color and luster were ever fresh
yajña-ghān rākṣasādīn parābhavaṃ nītvā
having defeated the demons and others who destroy sacrifices
yajñaṃ viṣṇum
Yajña, namely Viṣṇu, the Lord of sacrifice
entries.literal_english: In explaining the name Barhiṣmatī, he also praises the excellence of the region in two verses. Kuśa and kāśa grasses grew there, their green color ever fresh. The sages defeated demons and other destroyers of sacrifice and worshipped Yajña, Viṣṇu, the Lord of sacrifice.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact grouped source range preserved.
transliteration: barhiṣmatī nāma niruktiṃ bruvan prasaṅgād deśasya śraiṣṭhyam āha dvābhyām | kuśāḥ kāśāś cāsan | śaśvan nityaṃ haritaṃ varco varṇo yeṣām | yajña-ghān rākṣasādīn | parābhavaṃ nītvā yajñaṃ viṣṇum ||30||

entries.sanskrit: यज्ञ-पुरुषं विष्णुं यत इति यत्रायजत् । भुवं स्थानम् । लब्धेति तृन् प्रत्ययान्तम् । लब्धवान् सन्न् इत्य् अर्थः । यतो लब्धवांस् तं यज्ञ-पुरुषम् इति वा । एतेन स्वर्गाद् अपि भूमिः श्रेष्ठा, तत्रापि तत् स्थानं श्रेष्ठम् इत्य् उक्तं भवति ।
word_for_word: yajña-puruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ yata iti yatrāyajat
“Yatra” means “where”: he worshipped Viṣṇu, the Person of sacrifice.
bhuvaṃ sthānam
“bhuvam” means place
labdheti tṛn pratyayāntam
“Labdha” is formed with the tṛn suffix.
yato labdhavāṃs taṃ yajña-puruṣam iti vā
or, the sense is “having obtained that Person of sacrifice”
etena svargād api bhūmiḥ śreṣṭhā tatrāpi tat sthānaṃ śreṣṭham ity uktaṃ bhavati
By this it is said that the earth is superior even to heaven, and this place is best among places.
entries.literal_english: “Where he sacrificed to Viṣṇu, the Person of sacrifice”—“yatas” means “where.” “Bhuvam” means place. “Labdha” is formed with the kṛt suffix; it means “having obtained.” Or, the sense is “having obtained that Person of sacrifice.” Thus it is stated that the earth is superior even to heaven, and that among places this one is the best.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact grouped source range preserved.
transliteration: yajña-puruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ yata iti yatrāyajat | bhuvaṃ sthānam | labdheti tṛn pratyayāntam | labdhavān sann ity arthaḥ | yato labdhavāṃs taṃ yajña-puruṣam iti vā | etena svargād api bhūmiḥ śreṣṭhā, tatrāpi tat sthānaṃ śreṣṭham ity uktaṃ bhavati |

entries.sanskrit: प्रस्तुतम् आह---यां बर्हिष्मतीं नाम पुरीं समावसत् । पूर्वं यस्याम् उषितः, तस्यां निर्विश्य भवनं प्रविष्टः सन् भोगान् बुभुज इत्य् अन्वयः ॥३२॥
word_for_word: prastutam āha yāṃ barhiṣmatīṃ nāma purīṃ samāvasat
he returns to the subject: “the city named Barhiṣmatī, which he inhabited”
pūrvaṃ yasyām uṣitaḥ tasyāṃ nirviśya bhavanaṃ praviṣṭaḥ san bhogān bubhuja ity anvayaḥ
the construction is: having entered the house in the city where he had previously lived, he enjoyed its pleasures
entries.literal_english: He returns to the subject: “the city named Barhiṣmatī, which he inhabited.” The connection is: having entered that city where he had formerly lived, he enjoyed its pleasures.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact grouped source range preserved.
transliteration: prastutam āha---yāṃ barhiṣmatīṃ nāma purīṃ samāvasat | pūrvaṃ yasyām uṣitaḥ, tasyāṃ nirviśya bhavanaṃ praviṣṭaḥ san bhogān bubhuja ity anvayaḥ ||32||

entries.sanskrit: अन्येषां धर्मादीनाम् अविरोधेन । प्रत्य् उषेषु उषःसु सङ्गीयमाना सत्-कीर्तिर् यस्य, तथापि स्वयं हरेर् एव कथाः शृण्वन् भोगान् बुभुजे ।
word_for_word: anyeṣāṃ dharmādīnām avirodhena
without conflict with the other duties beginning with dharma
praty uṣeṣu uṣaḥsu saṅgīyamānā sat-kīrtir yasya
he whose good fame was sung every morning
tathāpi svayaṃ harer eva kathāḥ śṛṇvan bhogān bubhuje
yet he enjoyed his pleasures while listening only to the stories of Hari
entries.literal_english: Without conflict with the other duties beginning with dharma. Every morning his good fame was sung; yet he enjoyed his pleasures while listening only to the stories of Hari.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact grouped source range preserved.
transliteration: anyeṣāṃ dharmādīnām avirodhena | praty uṣeṣu uṣaḥsu saṅgīyamānā sat-kīrtir yasya, tathāpi svayaṃ harer eva kathāḥ śṛṇvan bhogān bubhuje |

entries.sanskrit: योग-मायासु ऐच्छिक-भोग-रचनासु । यद् यतः आभ्रंशयितुम् आ ईषद् अपि भ्रंशयितुम् अभिभवितुम् ॥३४॥
word_for_word: yoga-māyāsu aicchika-bhoga-racanāsu
“yogamāyāsu” means in the arrangements of desired enjoyments
yad yataḥ ābhraṃśayitum ā īṣad api bhraṃśayitum abhibhavitum
“yat yataḥ” is explained as “to cause to fall, even slightly,” that is, to overcome
entries.literal_english: “Yogamāyāsu” means in the arrangements of desired enjoyments. “Yat yataḥ” is explained as “to cause to fall, even slightly,” that is, to overcome.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact grouped source range preserved.
transliteration: yoga-māyāsu aicchika-bhoga-racanāsu | yad yataḥ ābhraṃśayitum ā īṣad api bhraṃśayitum abhibhavitum ||34||

entries.sanskrit: अतो यातो यामो यस्य पक्वस्यान्न् अस्य तद् गत-सारं भवति, अतोऽन्यद् अपि गत-सारं यात-यामम् उच्यते । अयात-यामा अगत-सारा आसन् । स्वान्तरं तदीयं मन्व्-अन्तरं यापयन्ति गमयन्ति ते यामाः कालावयवाः कुर्वतः स्व-वाक्यैर् उपनिबध्नतः ॥३५॥
word_for_word: ato yāto yāmo yasya pakvasyānn asya tad gata-sāraṃ bhavati
food that has passed its proper time loses its essence
ato’nyad api gata-sāraṃ yāta-yāmam ucyate
another thing whose essence has passed is also called “yātayāma”
ayāta-yāmā agata-sārā āsan
“ayāta-yāmāḥ” means fresh, whose essence has not departed
svāntaraṃ tadīyaṃ manv-antaraṃ yāpayanti gamayanti te yāmāḥ kālāvayavāḥ
“Yāmāḥ” are divisions of time that carry forward his own interval, namely the Manvantara
kurvataḥ sva-vākyair upanibadhnataḥ
of him who composes or recounts [the narratives] in his own words
entries.literal_english: The time of cooked food passes, and it loses its essence; hence anything whose essence has passed is called yātayāma. The time divisions were ayāta-yāmāḥ, fresh and without loss of essence. These yāmās—divisions of time—carry forward his own period, the Manvantara. This describes one who listens to and meditates on Viṣṇu, and who composes and speaks His narratives.

entries.sanskrit:
दिव्यास् त्वान्तरिक्षाः । मानुषाः शत्रु-प्रभवाः । भौतिकाः शीतोष्णादि-प्रभवाः । वैयासे ! हे विदुर
! ॥३७॥
word_for_word: divyās tvāntarikṣāḥ
the divine afflictions are those arising in the atmosphere
mānuṣāḥ śatru-prabhavāḥ
“mānuṣāḥ” means arising from human enemies
bhautikāḥ śītoṣṇādi-prabhavāḥ
“bhautikāḥ” means arising from material conditions such as cold and heat
vaiyāse he vidura
“O Vaiyāsa!” means “O Vidura, son of Vyāsa!”
entries.literal_english: The divine afflictions are those arising in the atmosphere; the human afflictions arise from enemies; the material afflictions arise from cold, heat, and the like. “O son of Vyāsa!” means “O Vidura!”
